bull_bear.body: D/E 0.34x; max comfort 1:1 consolidated (incl. renewable development projects). Finance cost down YoY. Asset monetization/offloading planned if leverage runs heavy (has solar/IPP assets). Disciplined, complementary diversification stance.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Govt-payment cycle:** AMRUT funds not released (5-6 states) → UBR ballooned to 195d, WC to 166d; recurring (Jal Jeevan last yr, AMRUT this yr). Some releases now confirmed (Chhattisgarh; coming for Rajasthan/Haryana/MP).
- **Order finalization delays / re-bidding:** elongated bid evaluation; a Nov-Dec L1 project went to re-bid (timeline lost, neutral outcome).
- **Commodity / geopolitical crisis:** raw-material/lithium-ion cost spike → 1-2pp margin pressure.
- **Guidance credibility:** missed FY26 35% guidance; investor explicitly asked for realistic targets — FY27 deliberately conservative.
- **OCF post-tax negative** (-INR63 cr); concentration on central-govt-funded projects (de-risking via NTPC B2B + private wind).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Candid on the miss — admitted revenue guidance not met, explained design-stage cost build-up, ECL/depreciation/IPP drags transparently. Conservative reframing of FY27 (42% conversion vs raw 75% growth). Took investor criticism on guidance realism gracefully. Confident but measured on renewables; disciplined leverage and capex discipline. Slightly defensive on "no margin compression" framing.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The headline "+75% FY27 growth" is an artifact of a tiny FY26 base; mgmt insists on viewing it as ~42% OB conversion — the real number to track is conversion rate, not growth %.
- FY26 ~95% order-to-order conversion but revenue still missed — the bottleneck is design/approval-to-execution lag, not order wins.
- Renewables grew from ~INR12 cr (till Dec) to INR117 cr in Q4 alone — entire FY26 renewable revenue (INR129 cr) was back-ended and ~0-margin (IPP), structurally depressing Q4 optics.
- UBR at 195 days (not receivables — receivables actually improved to 53d) is the true working-capital story; it's GST-invoice timing tied to govt fund release, so a release wave could sharply unwind WC.
- Company is quietly building T&D/transmission pre-quals via BESS execution — optionality not yet priced.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Group snapshot states a debt-equity ratio of 0.34; the annual key-ratio chart shows debt to equity of 0.5 (FY23), 0.8 (FY24), 0.2 (FY25) and 0.3 (FY26), with debt of ₹645 / 2,336 / 2,341 / 4,223 Mn over the same years.
- Net worth has scaled sharply — ₹1,286 Mn (FY23), ₹2,922 Mn (FY24), ₹9,945 Mn (FY25, the IPO year) and ₹12,327 Mn (FY26) — while return ratios have compressed as the equity base grew: ROE 57.8% → 39.3% → 17.8% → 15.3% and ROCE 44.4% → 33.1% → 17.6% → 17.3%.
- Long-term borrowings rose to ₹2,473 Mn (Mar-26) from ₹983 Mn (Mar-25) and short-term borrowings to ₹1,750 Mn from ₹1,359 Mn, funding the PP&E and CWIP build; total assets grew to ₹20,422 Mn from ₹14,983 Mn.
- Credit ratings of CRISIL A/Stable (long term) and CRISIL A1 (short term); the wind segment is described as carrying near-zero debt with TD/TNW of 0.10.
- Working capital and liquidity as at Mar-26: trade receivables ₹1,653 Mn (down from ₹2,057 Mn), cash and cash equivalents ₹520 Mn (down from ₹1,624 Mn), bank balances ₹2,833 Mn (down from ₹3,928 Mn), other current financial assets ₹6,913 Mn (up from ₹3,792 Mn). The deck states no dividend or buyback policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Water/WW EPC (core):** STP (per-MLD INR1-1.5 cr), CETP (INR2-15 cr/MLD, industry-dependent), WTP (INR30-50 lakh/MLD). Design = 2-5% of turnkey value. Mostly EPC; some STPs on HAM. Completed marquee projects: 100 MLD STP Jodhpur (IFAS + biogas power + UF), 55 MLD STP Varanasi (solar-on-reactor, India-first, NMCG-recognized), 25 MLD CETP Sarigam, 30 MLD STP Bhiwadi — raising pre-qualification for larger/complex plants.
- **O&M (Water/WW):** INR951 cr OB; 3-5% of revenue; higher margin than execution; growing in absolute terms YoY.
- **Renewables (1 yr old):** Execution OB INR2,051 cr + O&M/IPP INR1,079 cr. NTPC BESS EPC (incl. EHV transformers / HT transmission lines self-executed). Wind EPC via **Suyog Urja Ltd** (acquired) — serves A-to-AAA-rated private clients. Solar assets + IPP. Reported as separate company; segmental revenues to be disclosed separately going forward.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Core business is described as designing, construction, operation and maintenance of Water and Wastewater Treatment Plants (WWTPs) and Water Supply Scheme Projects (WSSPs), delivered through three models — EPC, Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) and O&M.
- All projects are backed by Central and State Government bodies, with execution experience in World Bank-funded projects and participation in AMRUT, NMCG (National Mission for Clean Ganga) and SBM (Swachh Bharat Mission) schemes; the deck cites 'institution-backed projects with structured payment mechanisms ensuring revenue visibility'.
- Clientele listed as NMCG, Jal Nigam, industrial clients, municipalities and Public Work Dept.; marquee water counterparties include Maharashtra Urban Development Department, MIDC, UP Jal Nigam, Bihar Urban Infrastructure Development Corporation and Municipal Corporation Bhopal.
- Renewables arm is positioned across the value chain — 'Developer + EPC Contractor' for solar and BESS (IPP + EPC execution model) and 'End-to-End EPC contractor' for wind — with the NTPC relationship described as 'a landmark in grid-scale energy storage' and a strategic shift into thermal-linked BESS.
- Wind segment self-described as 'Asset-light · near-zero debt · ready-to-build' with long-cycle visibility, a scalable wind BOP platform, TD/TNW of 0.10, AAA/A-rated counterparties and repeat orders.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Acquired Suyog Urja, a wind energy company, to expand the renewable portfolio; goodwill of ₹27 Mn and a non-controlling interest of ₹47 Mn (versus ₹(7) Mn) appear on the Mar-26 balance sheet.
- [Marquee renewable orders] 930 MWh BESS projects at 4 locations for NTPC (₹9,631 Mn), land/ROW/BOP including civil for CGE 30, an SPV of Continuum Green (₹2,075 Mn), 150 MWh BESS at Bihar for BSPGCL as BESS IPP (₹1,450 Mn), 29 MW (AC) Nagpur for MSEDCL (₹1,116 Mn) and 40 MW (AC) Odisha for SECI (₹645 Mn); wind ROW/civil work for ReNew, JSW Renew Energy (300 MW), Tata Power Renewable Energy, plus JSW 556 MW, ReNew 250 MW, Suzlon 50 MW and Vibrant Energy 25 MW projects.
- [Marquee water orders] STP & sewerage network Pune (₹4,976 Mn), 135 MLD STP Saharanpur for UP Jal Nigam (₹4,439 Mn), CETP Kolhapur upgradation with ZLD for MIDC (₹3,955 Mn), 20 MLD STP Bihar (₹3,483 Mn), STP & sewerage network Nashik (₹3,263 Mn), 60 MLD STP Bhopal (₹2,480 Mn), 60 MLD STP and sewerage scheme at Mathura (₹2,400 Mn) and 17+23 MLD STP Ramgarh, Jharkhand (₹2,054 Mn).
- [Government funding backdrop] Scheme outlay table (₹ Cr) shows JJM at 11,500 / 50,100 / 60,000 / 69,684 / 22,612 / 17,000 / 67,670, NMCG at 1,600 / 2,250 / 2,800 / 1,800 / 2,976 / 2,687 / 3,100 and AMRUT at 7,300 / 10,000 / 14,000 / 16,000 / 5,513 / 7,500 / 8,000 across FY20-21 actuals through FY26-27 budgeted; policy levers cited are AMRUT 2.0, Namami Gange, NRCP and NPCA. On the renewables side the deck cites India targets of 280 GW solar and 100 GW wind installed by 2030 with a 208 GWh BESS pipeline by 2030, installed solar of ~162 GW by June 2026 (26.3 GW added in H1 2026, +43% YoY), cumulative wind of 57.4 GW, a battery storage pipeline that has crossed 92 GWh backed by a ~₹5,400 crore VGF outlay (May 2026) for ~30 GWh of new capacity, and a non-fossil capacity share of 52% vs 30% in March 2015.
- [Revenue concentration] Q1FY27 state-wise sales mix is led by Maharashtra 29% (₹898 Mn), Madhya Pradesh 15% (₹646 Mn), Jharkhand 9% (₹338 Mn), Uttar Pradesh 9% (₹328 Mn), Chhattisgarh 8% (₹285 Mn) and Haryana 8% (₹275 Mn) — a marked shift from FY25 when Madhya Pradesh alone contributed ₹5,158 Mn.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: FY26 EBITDA margin 24.2% (mgmt says no real compression once normalized; Q4 18.7% optical due to 0-margin IPP revenue + ECL + depreciation + design-stage employee cost). FY27 EBITDA guided 21-22% (cut 1-2pp for commodity inflation). Price-variation clauses in most contracts offset PART of cost rises, not all. BESS EPC ~10% PAT (lithium-ion import cost pressure — deferring battery procurement, doing BOS/civil/electrical first).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this):** All-time-high total OB INR6,814 cr (exec INR4,800 cr). FY26 revenue INR1,145 cr (+7.5%, MISSED 35% guidance); FY26 EBITDA margin 24.2%, PAT INR188 cr. Q4 weakest margins (EBITDA 18.7%) on 0-margin IPP + ECL + depreciation + design-stage costs. Renewables now ~35-40% of OB (BESS 930+150 MWh from NTPC/Bihar; Suyog Urja wind-EPC acquired). WC blew out to 166d (UBR 195d) on AMRUT fund delays. FY27 guide: rev ~INR2,000 cr, PAT INR270-280 cr, EBITDA cut to 21-22%, order inflow ≥INR2,500 cr. D/E 0.34x.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- **FY27 revenue: ~INR2,000 cr** (vs INR1,145 cr FY26 — implies ~75% growth, but mgmt frames as ~42% conversion of INR4,800 cr execution OB, deliberately conservative). Split: Water/WW ~INR1,350 cr + Renewables ~INR650 cr.
- **FY27 PAT: INR270-280 cr; PAT margin ~13.5-14%** (blended).
- **FY27 EBITDA margin: LOWERED to 21-22%** (from earlier 22-24%) due to global commodity/geopolitical crisis (1-2pp hit; price-variation clauses cover only part).
- **FY27 order inflow target: at least INR2,500 cr** of fresh orders.
- **FY28: 35-40% topline growth** implied; ~INR2,500-2,800 cr revenue from remaining current OB — "FY27 & FY28 visibility clear on current OB."
- **Q1 FY27 color:** Better than Q1 FY26 (~INR250 cr) despite global crisis; no number given.
- **Renewables/BESS margin:** BESS EPC ~10% PAT; blended renewables 10-12% PAT.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

outlook.body:
- Execution OB INR4,800 cr; total OB INR6,814 cr (incl. O&M + IPP).
- Q4 additions: BUIDCO Bihar INR348 cr; Pune+Nashik sanitation (Swachh Bharat) INR824 cr; 4 NTPC BESS EPC projects (930 MWh, ~INR1,070 cr — UP/Assam/Karnataka/Telangana); acquired 150 MWh BESS project in Bihar.
- **Bid pipeline:** ~INR1,200 cr bids submitted + ~INR5,000 cr of projects of interest yet to bid.
- FY26 starting OB was only ~INR1,200 cr; converted INR1,145 cr (~95% conversion rate) — but revenue still missed because new wins stayed in design stage.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- BESS: positioning as first-mover in India's 90 GW battery-storage pipeline; 930 MWh NTPC + 150 MWh Bihar.
- Wind EPC (Suyog) into private A/AAA clients — de-risks govt receivables.
- Desalination optionality: MIDC CETP-ZLD textile project (UF/RO, one of India's biggest) builds pre-qualification to enter desalination (open to JVs).
- Water re-use / BOT: treated CETP/ZLD water recirculated to industry could become revenue stream / BOT model (preliminary).
- T&D EPC: NOT entering soon, but BESS work (EHV/HT lines) gives pre-quals; possible future diversification (AI-driven power demand cited).
- HAM/IPP annuity income — decent IRR, O&M absolute profitability rising.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Pure-play water/wastewater EPC missed FY26 revenue guidance (35%→7.5% growth) on slow order finalization + projects stuck in design stage, but pivots hard into renewables (BESS/wind/solar, now ~35-40% of order book) with all-time-high INR6,814 cr total order book giving ~24-month visibility — execution conversion (not order book) is the swing factor, and a global commodity crisis trims FY27 margin guidance.
